clue.text: Broadcast by top-notch Communist

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords
a Communist is a Red

explanation.surface: A news item transmitted by a leading Communist official.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that has gone out on radio or television has been aired.

clue.text: A man of the cloth, we declare

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: A clergyman speaks up for his congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A man of the cloth' suggests a priest, but here it is one who makes cloth on a loom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works a loom produces cloth, a playful reading of the clerical phrase.

clue.text: Pull out all the stops to leave the country

explanation.surface: Making a great effort before emigrating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something lavishly, while literally a country dweller heads for the town.

clue.text: Demo in support of international cricket

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a Test match is an international cricket fixture

explanation.surface: A demonstration backing the national cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a long-form international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a public demonstration of objection, a march or rally.

clue.text: Old-fashioned fellow bit the dust

parts.note: passé means out of date
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: An outdated man collapsed and died.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a lecturer or fellow at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are euphemisms for having died.

clue.text: Man of property may take in confessor

parts.note: being in means being at home
one who owns up to something is an owner in a playful sense

explanation.surface: A landlord might give lodging to a priest who hears confessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may take' is a link; 'confessor' is not a priest but someone who owns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding a house is a man of property in the literal sense.

clue.text: Squad taking regular meals in the dining room

parts.note: a team or side
board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A team being fed its daily meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition places the furniture rather than naming it: it is the cabinet found in the dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a serving cabinet typically kept where meals are eaten.

clue.text: A noble cut of beef

explanation.surface: An aristocrat being served a piece of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the lowest rank in Britain shares the name of a large double sirloin joint.

clue.text: I take a turn playing in "Othello"

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in having a go

explanation.surface: An actor says he is having his go on stage in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The villain of that Shakespeare tragedy is a role played in it.

clue.text: Fail to mention holiday abroad

parts.note: leave is time off work
out means away or out of doors, abroad in the old sense

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to say they spent their holiday overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to fail to say it.

clue.text: A Wren's problem re, quires solution

indicators.note: a problem means the letters are put into a troubled, rearranged state

explanation.surface: A naval servicewoman's puzzle needs to be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren is a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service. 'problem' signals rearranging WRENS into NSWER, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer to a puzzle is its solution.

clue.text: Consequently the mon, ster returned

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back and read the other way

parts.note: an ogre is a monster

explanation.surface: As a result, the beast came back.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, used in English to mean as a result.

clue.text: Escort to the cellar for final confrontation

parts.note: to show someone somewhere is to escort them
the cellar is down below

explanation.surface: Leading someone downstairs for a decisive fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A climactic clash that settles a dispute, as in a Western gunfight.

clue.text: Cook book dashed off to make money

definitions.text: book dashed off to make money

explanation.surface: A recipe book written quickly for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: someone who boils a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who heats a pan, and also a hack novel written only to earn a living.

clue.text: Daily fare for MPs

explanation.surface: Everyday food served to Members of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs sit in the lower house of the British Parliament; commons also means shared rations.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared daily rations of food, and the elected chamber of the UK Parliament.

clue.text: Doctor has to call-by car, clearly

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
to ring is to call by phone

explanation.surface: A doctor must make a house call driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling in an automobile is going by road in a vehicle.

clue.text: Vocalist without wife is a lively socialite

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the vocalist goes round the other letter

parts.note: a singer

explanation.surface: A singer whose wife is absent becomes a party animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashionable person who enjoys parties and nightlife.

clue.text: Hang around to get a plant

explanation.surface: Waiting about to acquire some greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A request to pause briefly, and a thorny shrub whose hooks catch passers-by.

clue.text: Attacking player who refuses to work

explanation.surface: A forward who will not do his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward in football, and a worker who downs tools in industrial action.

clue.text: Jack's pamphlet theoretical in nature

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, AB for able seaman, plus the possessive S
a tract is a pamphlet

explanation.surface: A sailor's leaflet is quite academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceptual rather than concrete or practical.

clue.text: A British and French consortium to help criminals

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: An Anglo-French business group assists lawbreakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist in wrongdoing, as in aiding and abetting.

clue.text: Tiny distance from a Scottish island

explanation.surface: A small gap separates us from an island in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small imperial measure of length, and a Scots word for a small island.

clue.text: Irritated when given only tea for nourish, ment

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
being given food for nourishment is being fed

explanation.surface: Annoyed at being given nothing but tea to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbed sore or annoyed.

clue.text: Did no work, but ticked over

explanation.surface: Someone loafed while their engine kept running.
explanation.definitionFit: Was lazy, and ran an engine slowly without engaging gears.

clue.text: Have a stab at exotic recipe

indicators.note: exotic means strange, so the letters are given an unusual order

explanation.surface: Trying out a foreign dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a stab at' looks like 'attempt' but means stab literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To puncture or go through with a point.

clue.text: Wild rice is grown there

explanation.surface: Wild rice cultivated in a flooded field.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a temper means furious, and rice grows in a flooded field.

clue.text: Miserly Pole acquires money

parts.note: mean means stingy
S is the South Pole

explanation.surface: A stingy Polish man comes into cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial resources, as in a person of means.

clue.text: Saved-from having to drag the shopping home?

definitions.text: from having to drag the shopping home?

explanation.surface: Spared carrying the groceries back yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescued, and brought to the door by a supplier.
